objective.primaryRule: the formal primary is the actual-profit role of the final selectable set at C24 (C4, E, A, B, C85, the independent shortlist and both informed shortlists): the highest development centre net among qualified members (gates Q1-Q6; fresh confirmation decides qualification), ties by the higher selection robust net, the lower centre DD, then the label. C4 is the user's preferred no-improvement fallback; a frozen prudent-recommendation rule replaces C4 only if the development replacement candidate (the highest-net qualified member dominating C4) passes V1-V3 and is supported across later periods (PROTOCOL.md §9.4).

risk.denominator: one fixed $100,000 principal budget (not peak account equity)

budget.notes: Distinct candidate proposals (centres): independent 131,072 base / 196,608 cap per cutoff × 4 cutoffs (C19, C21, C23, C24) = 524,288 base / 786,432 cap; informed fixed-D1 and joint lanes at C24 ≈ 21,800 base / ≈ 38,200 cap each; plus refinement moves (≈ 3,000-6,000 per cutoff). The figure above is the cap order of magnitude (≈ 830,000). Backend evaluations (centres + neighbours): ≈ 0.9-1.1 M per independent cutoff at base, ≤ ≈ 1.9 M at the cap (C24 door; earlier doors cheaper), informed ≈ 0.6-1.0 M, qualification ≈ 0.3 M; the order-of-magnitude cap is 8 M. Counted separately: screen centres, rung-1/2/3 and refinement centres and neighbours, qualification, folds, sequential, validation, retries, archive hits and worker compute time (PROTOCOL.md §7.4).
